perspective:
**Reconstruction of Harold Padilla’s available information, in first person:**

- I am Harold Padilla, a project manager. I know Arthur Begum as a police officer and as a friend/professional contact I rely on for advice and support.
- I felt frustrated and anxious because my project was not progressing well, and I believed my team was unmotivated.
- I arranged and attended a meeting with Arthur at a local coffee shop.
- I told Arthur that my project team seemed completely unmotivated and that it was affecting progress; I said I was at my wit’s end.
- I heard Arthur say that motivation can be tricky and that I should try understanding what drives each team member individually.
- I told Arthur I had not really done that and had been focusing on project goals and deadlines. I agreed to look into their personal motivations.
- I heard Arthur advise me to have one-on-one conversations with team members to see what was going on. I said I would try it and felt more hopeful.
- Afterward, I felt hopeful and relieved. I believed Arthur’s advice would help, and I decided to implement his suggestions in team meetings.
- I told my team I wanted to try quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. I heard Team Member 1 say that could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it.
- I told the team I would schedule time with each of them and said we should make the project a success together.
- I noticed the team still was not responding well despite using Arthur’s advice. I felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- I told Arthur I had tried his suggestions but the team still was not responding well, and I was worried about the project.
- I heard Arthur say there might be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that I might need to dig deeper.
- I told Arthur I had not thought of that and would set up another round of meetings to get to the bottom of it. I thanked him.
- I felt determined and focused. I believed there might be underlying team issues I had not addressed, so I held one-on-one meetings with team members to understand their concerns.
- I asked team members to share concerns or problems. I heard Team Member 1 say there was tension between a few team members that was affecting work.
- I heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed with the workload and stressed, which made it hard to stay motivated.
- I told them I would look into resolving conflicts and see if tasks could be redistributed to ease pressure. I told them their well-being was important to me.
- I felt optimistic and empowered. I believed addressing individual concerns would improve team performance, and I intended to create a more supportive and open team environment with regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- I announced those changes to the team. I heard Team Member 1 say it sounded great and would help, and Team Member 2 agree that it was good their concerns were being addressed.
- I said I was glad to hear that and told the team that their input and well-being were crucial to our success.

**Not available to me:** Arthur’s private/internal thoughts, team members’ unspoken motives, narrator-only explanations, and any events I did not observe or was not told about.
